headline_tag: Uptrend holds as price sits just above its 50-day line

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up the acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with high confidence (87/100 including today's news, 77 on market data alone), so this is a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is sitting right on its 50-day average, US stocks just had a rough week and the Fed meets on 27 October, grow the budget in steps and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $81,411 (the 50-day average). This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

reasons: Price is about 13% above its 200-day average and up 25% over 90 days.
About 68% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average.
Price sits just above its 50-day average ($81,411), below the $86,603 30-day high.
The 200-day average still slopes slightly down and price is 35% below its record.
watch: The longer picture leans up, but price is resting barely above its 50-day average ($81,411) after US stocks had their worst week since June, with the Fed deciding on 27 October. A close below $81,411 would test the uptrend; a move back above $86,603 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still leans up, but the coming days look undecided. Short term, the mood is mildly positive rather than excited: the Fear & Greed reading is a middling 53/100, and Bitcoin is about 2.5% lower than a week ago after US stocks had their worst week since June. If price closes above $86,603 (the 30-day high) it turns clearly up, a close below $81,411 (the 50-day average) turns it down, and in between it stays choppy. A return of calm in stocks would firm this up; a further slide there would weaken it, so time quick-reaction content to the news rather than to big promotions.

Over the next month, things still tilt up but more softly than earlier this month. Price is still about 25% above where it was three months ago, yet it has given back part of that gain and now rests barely above its 50-day average; news is nudging this a little lower, with MSCI warning it may drop Strategy, the biggest corporate Bitcoin buyer, from its global index, and France proposing a 31.4% tax on Bitcoin-to-stablecoin switches. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high), and the move fades if it closes below $81,411 (the 50-day average). The Fed decision on 27 October is the next scheduled test; a steady result would help, a surprise would hurt.

Over the next three to six months, the trend leans up: price is about 13% above its 200-day average and about 68% of the last 90 days closed above it, though that average itself is still sloping slightly down, so this is an early recovery rather than a settled uptrend. News adds a little here, as Charles Schwab opened direct Bitcoin buying to all its clients. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,499 (the 200-day average), with $66,979 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. The average turning upward would confirm it; that supports paying for steady growth campaigns aimed at active traders.

team_notes.marketing: Keep growing in steps: the longer picture leans up and no rally or drop window is open, so run steady campaigns for active traders rather than urgent pushes. Lead this week's content with mainstream access stories like Schwab and the 27 October Fed decision.
